etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English obligen, from Old French obligier, obliger, from Latin obligō, obligāre, from ob- + ligō. Doublet of obligate, taken straight from Latin.
senses: (transitive) To constrain someone by force or by social, moral or legal means.
(transitive, intransitive) To do (someone) a service or favour (hence, originally, creating an obligation).
